subject: Onboarding preflight: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — questions & checklist
messages:
From: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@acme-health.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: it@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy preflight — a few immediate questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're preparing a room for the Redwood private deployment and want to run a short preflight so we don't waste either team's time on the kickoff call. A few quick items we need clarified before we schedule network engineers: 

- Which TCP/UDP ports are required for agent -> control plane and for node-to-node traffic? Will we need any non-standard outbound access?
- Do you require inbound firewall rules to our VPC for health checks or callbacks?
- KMS: does Redwood expect us to provide a key in our KMS/HSM or will you manage encryption in the private control plane?
- Is there an expected maintenance window pattern and whether the private control plane pushes updates automatically?

If you can point us to a short checklist (or send the canonical preflight doc) we can triage items with our infra team before the call.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Systems Architect, Acme Health

--
Acme Health | 1-800-ACMEIT
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@acme-health.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight — a few immediate questions

Rajesh — appreciate the clear questions. Attaching our lightweight preflight checklist (PDF) and a draft topology image so your infra team can eyeball port and routing needs. Short answers here, and I'll add detail in the doc: 

- Ports: control-plane (443/HTTPS) outbound from customer nodes; mutual TLS (mTLS) on 443 for control-plane authentication. Node-to-node GPU traffic uses configurable high ports; default overlay range is 10000-20000/tcp but we can pin to a smaller set if you prefer.
- Inbound rules: generally no inbound firewall rules required for the control plane; health probes are pulled from the control plane over outbound connections, but if you want an optional management endpoint for diagnostics we can request a short-lived inbound rule.
- KMS: we support both models. If you bring a customer key (KMS/HSM), Redwood will encrypt model keys with your key. Otherwise we can manage keys in the private control plane but with stricter contractual controls.
- Updates: private control plane supports both automatic and manual update modes. For regulated orgs we recommend manual approvals during a scheduled maintenance window.

I'll let Dev and Marissa jump into port pinning and the deployment sizing notes. Can we aim for a 30-minute preflight on Wednesday 11/12 at 11:00am PST? If that works I'll send a calendar invite with the checklist linked.

Warmly,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: dev.patel@redwood.com <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, Rajesh Menon <r.menon@acme-health.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight — a few immediate questions

Adding a few implementation notes from infra: 

- Node egress: Your nodes must allow outbound 443 to the private control-plane IP range (we'll provide the /28) and outbound to our artifact CDN (S3 endpoints) on 443. If you have strict allow-lists, list both ranges.
- Overlay ports: we prefer to keep overlay ports 10000-10010/tcp for inter-node KV/cache traffic to reduce ACL surface; if you need, we can move to 20000-20005 to avoid clash with existing services.
- NTP/Time sync: ensure all nodes can reach your internal NTP or an approved time source; token expirations rely on clock skew < 10s.
- KMS integration: For HSM-backed keys, we need an IAM role/service-account with key-decrypt permission and a short-term credential exchange path (we can provide Terraform snippet).

I'll paste a minimal port list below for your firewall/ACL team to copy: 

- Outbound TCP 443 to control-plane (mutual TLS)
- Outbound TCP 443 to artifact/cdn endpoints (S3)
- TCP 10000-10010 (inter-node overlay)
- UDP 123 (NTP) or outbound to your internal NTP

Let us know if Acme requires IP allow-listing; we can provision static egress IPs for the control-plane side.

- Dev

Thanks Dev — that's a helpful port list. A couple of clarifying items from our security team after a quick read of the checklist: 

1) Can you confirm the control-plane /28 will be static for the lifetime of the deployment? We need to add it to our egress allow list and prefer a static mapping.
2) For KMS key rotation: who initiates rotation and how are key access audits surfaced to us?
3) For the artifact CDN: do you support a VPC endpoint (AWS) or do we need to open S3 endpoints publicly?

We can confirm Wed 11/12 11:00am PST — our infra lead Kelly will attend. I'll accept the invite when you send it.

—Rajesh
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@acme-health.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight — a few immediate questions

Rajesh — answering inline: 

1) Control-plane IPs: we can provision either a stable /28 for the control-plane egress or operate through a small pool of static IPs; for contractual/allow-listing purposes we can commit to a set of static IPs for the duration of the contract and put that in the onboarding worksheet.

2) KMS rotation: if you supply the KMS key, you control rotation and we will only be able to wrap/unlock using that key. Audit logs for decrypt operations are available from your KMS provider (CloudTrail logs for AWS KMS) and we also emit an audit event in our control-plane with a reference id. We'll include the exact log field mapping in the onboarding doc.

3) Artifact delivery: we support S3 VPC endpoints — we can provide the bucket ARNs and VPC endpoint policy snippets. You should not need to open S3 publicly.

Couple of next steps: Hannah — can you send the calendar invite and attach the Doc link for our onboarding worksheet? Rajesh — can Kelly paste any existing firewall rules that might conflict with overlay ports so Dev can propose an alternate range?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

- Redwood will provide a small static IP pool for control-plane egress (we'll confirm exact /28 by kickoff).
